summary: The entry contrasts active giving birth (II/III) with the born meaning in an already present II Detransitive box. Explicit Detransitive numbering repairs the missing gloss without inferring an agent.

Preterit-wa mwaladwalle places the goats’ birth before the theft; mwaldo narrates an accomplished birth at 112/108 and a prospective one at 112/105 or 113/216. Translation tense does not select the box.

The related wlḏ entry, consulted through the allowed lookup, has the same etymology, III mawlaḏle/mawləḏ and a Detransitive mtawləd note. The relationship warrants editorial collation, not automatic merging or redistribution of forms.

Keep round-1 wld II/III bases and its II Detransitive proposal. Unprefixed mawlad-/mwalad- birth predicates remain provisionally under II by the existing entry; prefixed mitawləd/kmimawləd is provisionally under III. This is not a normalized unified paradigm.
Active III Infectum and Infectum-wa are newly documented with mothers as actors and a purpose clause after pain-inducing treatment. Their mawl- vocalism is preserved.

The Caesar passage supplies a predicative born form contrasted with brought out. Its proposed Part. Pass. filing is morphological evidence from a folk explanation, not endorsement of the historical etymology.
No new productive Infinitiv is inferred from walade or təwlido in surrounding context; these are not separately supplied occurrences in this job.
Collate wld and wlḏ: do d/ḏ and mwal-/mawl- distinguish stems/dialects, or reflect source spelling? Preserve both entries until that is established.
Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/2: is Mawlaḏnowo verbal Detransitive Preterit-wa, a birth adjective plus past copula, or another segmentation? This box remains unestablished.
MAC Ishaq/4, MAC YT/1 and 98/1: confirm mawladno/moladno relative to existing mwaləd. The latter is provisionally filed by analogy, without normalising its vowels.
113/97 and 113/217: determine whether mawlodo and walade are productive Infinitiv forms or independent event nouns; walade alone cannot identify the stem.
113/217: verify whether mawldo differs morphologically from II mwaldo in the immediately preceding verse.
113/97: resolve the two -la elements in mawladlala; preserve the source ending without inventing a second participant.
Jan English is project machine translation; obtain native/editorial confirmation for the added examples.
Confirm wld/wlḏ and II/III allocation, especially mawlədəd second-person -əd, mawəldo and the prefixed kmimawləd. These spellings do not warrant automatic merger.
Jan 2.31/4993 has literal <...> gaps around nomuso and firstborn. Recover the source before using it as clean textual evidence; the quotation preserves all gaps.
At Jan 2.33/5389, are the unexpressed actors mothers or birth attendants? A distinct technical sense is withheld.
Jan 2.33/5389 may describe delivering children with assistance, but no midwife actor is expressed. It does not independently establish a technical assist-in-childbirth sense beyond giving birth.
Jan supports the round-1 born meaning with first-/second-person biographies, Christ and Julius, and a birth-result property. New participants and biographical dates are not new senses.
